obligations.text: Extract a bit field using only the low eight bits of the unsigned position and length operands. Zero length gives zero. Unsigned padding is zero. Signed padding uses the last extracted bit, or input bit 31 when the field reaches beyond the input. Positions past bit 31 can therefore give all ones for negative signed inputs. The normative syntax supports u32/s32; the source example spelling bfe.b32 is not admitted. Introduced PTX 2.0; requires sm_20. All 32-bit input words and source/destination aliases are allowed.
Evaluate sources in the incoming state before writing the destination; permit repeated sources and source/destination aliases. Only the selected word register and incremented program counter change.
Both positive and negative instruction guards are supported. A false guard skips the write and advances only the program counter. The selected operations have no additional predicate operands.

The occurrence identifies the fetched instruction and original program counter. Enabled syntactic reads include guard then word operands then predicate operands, retaining repeats. Disabled instructions read only the guard. No memory effect is claimed.
Target slice: ISA exactly 94, numeric SM at least 20, including false guarded steps. This is a feature requirement, not GPU name validation.

Exactly bfe.u32, bfe.s32 with word-register destination then 3 word sources in field order. Preserve guards. Malformed known spellings return invalidOperands; all other names return unsupportedMnemonic. Decode succeeds iff the statement is the encoding. Compatible declarations and immediate conversion are supplied; no raw parser claim.

Universal transition, frame, deterministic result, one-step existence and origin theorems must follow the actual definitions without excluding aliases or input bit patterns. Absence of raw module parsing, declared-register checking and whole-kernel termination is within the deliberate scope.

scope: Selected bfe.u32, bfe.s32 leaf only; all other spellings, widths, options, raw parsing and hardware correspondence are outside scope. Existing support files are fixed.
